new_entities.name: Hydrolysed collagen peptides
new_entities.description: Orally consumed hydrolysed collagen peptide supplements marketed for skin, joint, and connective tissue support.

new_entities.name: Clinical skin elasticity
new_entities.description: Clinically measured or instrument-measured skin elasticity in human trials.

edges.effect_quant: Across 26 randomized trials involving 1,721 participants, oral hydrolysed collagen significantly improved skin elasticity versus placebo, and two additional meta-analyses reached the same directional conclusion in pooled cohorts of 967 and 1,125 participants.
edges.population: mostly adult women with visible skin aging or cosmetic concerns taking oral hydrolysed collagen for roughly 8 to 24 weeks
edges.mechanism: Hydrolysed collagen peptides may support dermal extracellular matrix turnover and water-binding properties, with downstream effects on collagen density and elastic behavior of the skin.
edges.summary: This is one of the cleaner consumer-aesthetic supplement edges. Multiple modern meta-analyses converge on modest but repeatable improvement in skin elasticity after a few months of oral hydrolysed collagen supplementation.
edges.caveats: Most trials are industry-adjacent and concentrate on women seeking anti-aging benefits, so the effect is better interpreted as cosmetic improvement rather than structural reversal of aging. The absolute effect size is usually modest, not transformative.

evidence.notes: Effects of Oral Collagen for Skin Anti-Aging: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence.citation: deMirandaRB et al 2021 Int J Dermatol
evidence.notes: Effects of hydrolyzed collagen supplementation on skin aging: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
